r: The **Rashtrakutas** – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta"; early emblem **Garuda**
Feudatories of the **Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas** – emblem **Varaha** (changed by **Prola I**); title **Mahamandaleswara**, borne by Beta II
Only issued the Magallu grant; never Kakatiya overlords
Samanta (feudatory) 956–1162 → **sovereign 1163–1323**; ruled Andhra in the **12th–13th centuries**
Hoysalas (10th–11th c.), Gahadavalas (11th c.), Kakatiyas and Yadavas (12th c.) – none in the early 8th century
The **Kakatiyas** ruled the eastern Deccan in the 12th–14th c.; the Seunas held the west
**First mention** of the Kakatiyas – Kakatiya **Gundyana** (Kakara Gundana)
Best genealogy; line begins with **Venna (Venna Bhupati)**
Names **Beta I** as the **first Kakatiya king**; records the accession of **Durga Nripathi**
**Hanamkonda (Anumakonda) Vishaya**, received by Beta I through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**
Rashtrakuta Krishna made Gundaya's son **Eriya** its head – a check on the **Mudigonda Chalukyas**; part of their kingdom near Orugallu
Early **Kakatiya** seat with **Orugallu (Warangal)** on its border; **Eriya Rashtrakuta** ruled it from **Orugallu Kakatipuram**, his capital
The title **Kakatipuravallabha** (Bayyaram inscription period) links the clan name to **Kakatipuram**, likely after its **Kakatamma (Kakitamma) temple**
The Kakatiyas were initially **Jains** and later **Shaivas**
**Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva**
The **second dynasty after the Satavahanas** (the first major Andhra dynasty) to unite all Telugu lands; "gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism" – the **ultimate design to Andhra culture**
**P.V. Parabrahma Sastry**: **Kannada (Chalukya) rule in Andhra ended** with the Kakatiya kingdom
Developed Hanamkonda; Swayambhu temple in Orugallu
**Completed the fort** and **transferred the capital** from Hanumakonda to **Orugallu**; called it **Andhranagari**
Credited to **Ganapatideva**; the Bekkallu inscription (1195) already calls Orugallu **Rudradeva**'s capital, so Rudradeva is also credited
Construction **begun by Rudradeva**, completed by Ganapatideva, strengthened by Rudramadevi
"Single rock" – the ancient name of **Warangal**; the place that best reflects the Kakatiya contribution to culture (fort, Thousand Pillar temple, Ramappa nearby)
First to come to Hanamkonda; attacked **Kanchi (1051)** for **Someshwara I**
Made Anumakonda capital; Garuda → Varaha; **Kesari Samudram**
Saiva, initiated by Rameswara Pandita of Srisailam
**Victory pillar at Srisailam**; killed by the **Velanati Chodas**; Yadava conflict began
Invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva; died on an elephant crossing a river
Son of **Gundyana**; the **Vamsakartha** of the Kakatiyas; title **Kakati Puradhinatha**; his son Prola Raju bore **Kakati Vallabha**

Minister of **Beta II** (**Beta Raju II**, titles **Tribhuvanamalla** and **Vikrama Chakri**), a master of politics; with his help Beta II subdued **Paramara Jagadeva of Kollipaka** and **Medaraju of Polavasa**
Defeated the Kalachuri confederacy (Mailagi, Medaraja, Dommaraja) in **1159**, the **Telugu Chodas** and **Tailapa III**
Recorded in the **Draksharama** inscription (1158) of minister Inangala Brahmi Reddi
**Rudradeva handed over the kingdom to Mahadeva**, who took the throne after Rudra was captured by the Yadavas
**Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya** ("founder of the Kakati Rajya"), Raya Pitamahanka
**Kakatiya**; **UNESCO World Heritage Site 2021**; **floating bricks**; star-shaped platform
**1199–1262** (about **63 years**, the longest); first inscription **Manthena, 26 Dec 1199**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**
Held captive by Yadava **Jaitugi**; **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him
Brought **the whole Telugu area under one rule** after the Satavahanas, from Ganjam to Kanchi; largely restored the **political unity of the Telugu country** – the **greatest Kakatiya**
The most powerful Kakatiya, who **extended the empire up to Kanchi**
**Velanadu:** coastal campaign – general **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**; Ganapati married **Narama and Perama**, daughters of **Pinnachodi**, and made their brother **Jayapa** **Gajasahani**
**Nellore:** his forces invaded the Nellore Telugu Chola kingdom, defeated **Tammasiddhi**, handed the throne to **Thikkabhupala** (Tikka, father of Manumasiddhi), then marched on **Kanchi**
With **Choda Tikka** of Nellore killed **Prithviswara** → Velanati kingdom ended (title **Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda**)
With Akkana and Bayyana killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** – final end of the Velanati Chodas
**Jatavarman Sundara Pandya** beat the Kakatiyas at **Muttukur** (Nellore); **Nellore fell to the Pandyas**
Restored **Manumasiddhi II** after the poet **Tikkana** came as envoy; Tikkana dedicated **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**
Fought the **Eastern Gangas** for southern Kalinga and Vengi
**Ramappa temple** (Recherla Rudra, 1213), **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks, **Ganapavaram** villages, **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (1244)
**Telugu replaced Sanskrit** in inscriptions from his reign
No son; **two daughters**, **Rudramadevi** and **Ganapamba (Ganapamadevi)**; sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married the sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**
**Succeeded him**, raised as a son (putrika), trained by her mother **Kupama Devi**; married **Veerabhadra** of the **Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas**
Defeated the Pandyas, Eastern Gangas and Seunas
Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya; source for Prolaraja's history
Independence; Prola II's conquests; composed by **Achitendru**, found by **J.S. Fleet**
Beta I first king; Durga Nripathi's accession

4.x: **June 2026:** an ASI survey of the **Nallamala** copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records of the 2nd–16th c.

r: Conflict began under **Prola II**; **Jaitugi** killed Rudradeva and held Ganapati; Mahadeva died in the revenge war; Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava Mahadeva
Veera Ballala II's advance made Jaitugi free Ganapati; Prataparudra's commander **Pedarudru** beat **Ballala III** after 1316
**Malik Kafur** besieged Warangal in **1310** (tributary); **1323** fall; Prataparudra **died jumping into the Narmada** (Musunuri record)

5.x: **Legacy:** one tradition makes **Harihara and Bukka** treasury officers of **Prataparudra II** who fled to **Kampili** after 1323; the **Nayankara system** was carried on by Vijayanagara.
